answer_1.quote: Generating summaries with different language styles can benefit readers of varying literacy levels or interests. Significant progress has been made in abstractive summarization with large pre-trained Transformers.
answer_1.outputs: summaries with controlled styles (simplicity or ideological leaning)

answer_2.quote: Key metrics include simplicity level estimated by our scorer and Dale-Chall readability. We use GPT-2 perplexity to measure fluency, and BERTScore for content preservation.

answer_4.quote: We recruit three fluent English speakers to evaluate system summaries for informativeness ... and fluency ... on a scale of 1 (worst) to 5 (best). They then rank the summaries by simplicity level (ties are allowed).
answer_4.guideline: Raters evaluate informativeness (coverage of important information) and fluency (grammaticality) on a 1-5 scale, then rank summaries by simplicity; for headlines, they score relevance on a 1-5 scale and identify ideological stances.
